cards.explanation: The answer is to go and present himself to Ahab. The LORD tells Elijah, the prophet, "Go and present yourself to Ahab…" (1 Kings 18:1). Ahab is Israel's king, and he's the very man Elijah told about the drought (1 Kings 17:1). That's a walk straight into the lion's den, and Elijah just goes. I would have needed a minute and a cookie.

The answer is rain! The LORD tells Elijah, "…I will send rain upon the face of the earth." In the third year of the drought, that's the best sentence anybody could hear. Notice who does the sending, friends. The LORD says, "…I will send…"

The answer is True. The text says Obadiah "…greatly feared the LORD…" He's in charge of the palace of a king who has turned from the LORD, and he still honors Him. That's a man holding steady in a hard place.

The answer is cave. Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them fifty men per cave. He also kept them supplied with food and water. A hundred prophets, two caves, and one busy palace man with a very secret errand.

The answer is grass to keep the horses and mules alive. Ahab says, "Perhaps we will find grass to keep the horses and mules alive so that we will not have to destroy any livestock." The famine is so severe that the king's animals are at risk. Even the king is out searching every spring and valley for something green.

The answer is False, and the text is plain about it. They divided the land to explore. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went the other way by himself. No side by side here, friends. Keep that in mind, because Obadiah ends up on his own when something surprising shows up.
The answer is True. When Obadiah recognizes Elijah, he falls facedown. Then he asks, "Is it you, my lord Elijah?" Obadiah calls him "my lord," and I think the facedown part says he was shocked.
The answer is False. Elijah tells Obadiah, "Go tell your master, ‘Elijah is here!’…" That's an announcement, not a secret. Elijah wants Ahab to hear it.

The answer is that Ahab will put him to death. That's what Obadiah fears. He asks, "How have I sinned, that you are handing your servant over to Ahab to put me to death?" He's not worried about a scolding, friends. In his mind, this message could cost him his life.

The answer is True. Obadiah says that when they said, "He is not here…" Ahab "…made that kingdom or nation swear that they had not found you." The king wasn't just asking around. He wanted that kingdom's oath, and that's how hard he searched.

The answer is that the Spirit of the LORD may carry him off. That's Obadiah's worry. He says, "I do not know where the Spirit of the LORD may carry you off when I leave you." Then he spells out the problem. If Ahab comes and doesn't find Elijah, "…he will kill me." So he's afraid of an empty spot where Elijah was supposed to be.

The answer is today! Elijah says, "As surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will present myself to Ahab today." That answers Obadiah's worry about Elijah vanishing (1 Kings 18:12). Elijah puts the LORD's life behind his word. I think that would settle my nerves a little.

The answer is Ahab and his father's house. Elijah says, "I have not troubled Israel, but you and your father's house have…" He hands the title right back to the king. That's like someone handing you back a bill you were sure was theirs.

The answers are commandments and Baals. Elijah says Ahab and his father's house "…have forsaken the commandments of the LORD…" That's the real trouble he names, friends. The king called Elijah the troubler, and Elijah answered with this. Then he says they "…have followed the Baals." The Baals are false gods, so they walked away from the LORD's commandments and followed those instead.

The answer is Mount Carmel. Elijah tells Ahab to summon all Israel to meet him on Mount Carmel. He also names who should come with them. The one who was being searched for is now picking the meeting place.

The answer is Jezebel's. Elijah says the four hundred prophets of Asherah "…eat at Jezebel’s table." Jezebel is Ahab's wife (1 Kings 16:31). Elijah also names the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal, but the table is mentioned with the prophets of Asherah.
